hypothesis: Compressed batch encoding allocates a fresh section BytesMut (doubling from zero), fresh compressor outputs (doubling from zero), and - for snappy - a second framing copy; pre-sizing outputs with Java's size/2 estimate, flooring the section at 1 KiB, framing snappy in place, and reusing both buffers in a bounded worker scratch cuts per-codec allocs.
limits: Wall-clock bytes/s shows no distinguishable change: paired medians range -9.9%..+5.4% but the noise floor (untouched decompress paths swing -6.4%..+2.6%, signs flip across entropies sharing identical code paths) dominates. Acceptance rides the deterministic route (allocs -28..-36%).
Instruction-count gate is Linux-only (ci-perf-gate.sh SKIP on Darwin); Ir impact left for Linux CI. The change removes allocations and a memcpy without adding work, so Ir is expected to fall or hold.
Exact section pre-sizing deliberately left to KL09-32 (one-pass sizing owns that mechanism); the 1 KiB floor composes with it (reserve is a no-op under exact sizing).

No compressed nb-produce cell exists to show worker-scratch steady-state on nb lanes; scratch steady-state measured by a throwaway second-use census (deleted before commit): warm gzip 8, snappy 1, lz4 3 allocs (compressor-internal state only; section/packed/output growth zero). Fresh-encoder internal state intentionally out of scope (deliverable covers output buffers).
